text:
maria-ops: heads up — got a 5xx-fraction SLO alert from probe in us-west-2 at 03:14 UTC. dashboard shows a ~2.8% bump for ~6m. not seeing customer error spikes yet.
ashok: I see the alert. is it probe-only or are real requests affected?
jordan: probe-only so far per the traffic split panel. production 5xx stays ~0.3%.
maria-ops: exact probe query returned: probe/ingress 5xx fraction = 2.8% over 5m, count = 320 errors. alerting rule fired on fraction crossing 2.5% for 5m.
eli: could be health-checks or internal test traffic leaking into probes. any unusual user-agent in logs?
maria-ops: quick grep shows a spike of requests with UA: "Redwood-Client/1.0 (prefetcher)". many of those are returning 502 and 504.
jordan: ah — that matches the dedicated prefetch job we rolled last week. maybe it started hitting new gateway path and timing out.
maria-ops: running a logql filter to confirm:
```
{job="ingress"} | json | user_agent =~ "Redwood-Client.*prefetcher" | status >= 500 | count_over_time(5m)
```
eli: also check traces for those traces — I suspect missing trace_id for many of those which creates gaps in our tail analysis.
maria-ops: yeah many entries have trace_id null. deploy-bot: deploy rolled: prefetcher v2.1.0 to canary at 02:58 UTC.
ashok: repro hypothesis: prefetcher is opening large batch requests (seq_len=4096 style) causing backend model workers to stall -> proxy queues -> gateway returns 504. support-bot: have two customer tickets mentioning intermittent timeouts from 03:00-03:20 UTC. maybe overlapping.
jordan: quick repro (dev):
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "User-Agent: Redwood-Client/prefetcher" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x","max_tokens":4096,"batch_size":64}' -v
```
expected to see backend queueing and gateway returns 504.
eli: mitigation idea: exclude internal prefetcher UA from probe alerts (temporary) and add absolute error count threshold to avoid fraction-only noise. also add a rule to ignore requests with missing trace_id for the specific alert.
maria-ops: proposed alert update: fire only when `5m_fraction > 2.5%` AND `5m_error_count > 500` OR `5m_sustained_fraction > 2.5% for 15m` — this reduces noisy short blips.
jordan: agree. also add a dashboard tile: 5xx-by-user_agent and 5xx-missed-traces to help triage.
ashok: long-term: make prefetcher respect our rate limits and add client-side backoff; also ensure trace header propagation. I'll open an infra ticket assigned to @ashok.
maria-ops: for immediate triage steps (runbook):
1) confirm prefetcher canary status and roll back if error rate continues.
2) temporarily mute probe channel alert for UA filter: `user_agent:prefetcher`.
3) run trace gap query: `sum(rate(trace_id_missing[5m])) by (service)` and escalate if > 1% of requests.
4) share curl repro with model infra oncall.
ashok: started infra ticket INF-4221 and pinged model-oncall.
maria-ops: rolled temporary mute on alert rule and added exclusion filter. will monitor for 10m.
eli: can we also add a sampling policy so prefetcher traces are kept (even if noisy) to avoid trace gaps?
jordan: yes, request sampling tweak can be done in the gateway config; I'll draft a small patch.
maria-ops: update — after mute the probe fraction dropped to 0.4% and customer tickets still show isolated 504s but not widespread. leaving monitoring on.
support-bot: support cases linked: CASE-12982, CASE-12983. customers asked for ETA — we replied: investigating prefetcher canary.
maria-ops: follow-ups: ashok to coordinate prefetcher rollback or throttling, jordan to PR sampling + dashboard, eli to chase trace header propagation fix. I'll keep this thread updated and convert to a postmortem if it recurs. :thumbsup:
